{"name": "run_python", "arguments": {"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Check premises
print("Shape:", df.shape)
print("Unique values in converted:", df['converted'].unique())
print("Count of -1 in customer_age:", (df['customer_age'] == -1).sum())
print("Sample of customer_age:", df['customer_age'].sample(5).values)

# Verify that -1 is used as sentinel for missing age
# (already known from documentation, but confirm)
assert (df['customer_age'] == -1).sum() == 108, "Expected 108 missing age values (sentinel -1)"
assert df['converted'].isin([0, 1]).all(), "converted should only be 0 or 1"

# Check revenue format and clean it
print("Revenue sample:", df['revenue'].sample(5).values)
# Strip commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check for QA orders
qa_orders = df[df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print("Number of QA orders:", len(qa_orders))

# Check for refunded orders
refunded = df[df['status'] == 'refunded']
print("Number of refunded orders:", len(refunded))

# But for this question, we only care about converted customers and their age
# So we filter to converted == 1
converted_df = df[df['converted'] == 1]

# Now check age: -1 is missing, so exclude those
converted_valid_age = converted_df[converted_df['customer_age'] != -1]

# Compute mean age
mean_age = converted_valid_age['customer_age'].mean()
print(f"Mean age of converted customers (excluding -1): {mean_age}")

# Output for report
mean_age"})
